content.raw_text: GENEVA — After seventeen grueling rounds of negotiation spanning more than three years, delegations from the three neighboring republics signed a comprehensive peace agreement at the Palais des Nations on Wednesday, formally concluding a border conflict that had displaced nearly two million civilians since 2019.
content.search_text: THE GLOBAL HERALD > Historic Peace Accord Signed in Geneva GENEVA — After seventeen grueling rounds of negotiation spanning more than three years, delegations from the three neighboring republics signed a comprehensive peace agreement at the Palais des Nations on Wednesday, formally concluding a border conflict that had displaced nearly two million civilians since 2019.

breadcrumb: THE GLOBAL HERALD > Historic Peace Accord Signed in Geneva

content.raw_text:
DECADES OF CONFLICT END
The treaty, brokered by a coalition of neutral mediators from five nations, establishes a demilitarized zone spanning 40 kilometers along the contested highland frontier and creates an independent verification commission staffed by 600 international observers. Both armies must complete withdrawal within 90 days.
